The evidence overwhelmingly shows mid-market and enterprise segments outperform SMB/startup segments across key operational metrics:

1. **Superior retention (lower churn):** The Q2 2026 KPI table shows monthly logo churn of 4.8% for SMB, 2.1% for Mid-market, and 1.3% for Enterprise [NL-012#NL-012-S03]. This is corroborated by David Okafor's analytics review stating "Mid-market and enterprise have significantly better retention" [NL-015#NL-015-S03]. The official segment characteristics table confirms these exact churn figures [NL-001#NL-001-S04].

2. **Higher customer satisfaction (NPS):** NPS scores are 31 for SMB, 47 for Mid-market, and 52 for Enterprise [NL-012#NL-012-S03]. David's analysis notes "Mid-Market at 2.1% and Enterprise at 1.3%... their NPS in Enterprise is 52 and Mid-Market is 47, whereas SMB is only 31" [NL-015#NL-015-S03]. The same metrics appear in the segment table [NL-001#NL-001-S04].

3. **Greater expansion revenue:** SMB generated $18,000 in expansion revenue, Mid-market $64,000, and Enterprise $91,000 (52.6% of all expansion revenue) [NL-012#NL-012-S03]. David Okafor explicitly compares these figures: "Mid-market generated $64,000 in expansions and Enterprise generated $91,000, whereas SMB only brought in $18,000" [NL-015#NL-015-S03]. The expansion dataset confirms the largest expansion events occur in enterprise accounts [NL-012#NL-012-S05].

4. **Disproportionate revenue share:** Mid-market and enterprise combined generate 83.8% of recurring revenue [NL-016#NL-016-S03].

5. **Superior unit economics:** Enterprise LTV:CAC ratio is 16.0x (LTV > $350,000, CAC $22,000) versus SMB's 8.3x (LTV capped at $25,000, CAC $3,000) [NL-016#NL-016-S03]. Enterprise contracts average $112,000 in ACV, making them the most valuable segment [NL-011#NL-011-S08].

6. **Higher Net Revenue Retention (NRR):** Overall NRR is 116%, driven by enterprise and mid-market accounts that "stick around" [NL-015#NL-015-S03]. This is corroborated by the note that "mid-market and enterprise segments demonstrate the highest Net Revenue Retention (116%)" [NL-023#NL-023-S03].

The text explicitly summarizes this: "customer satisfaction (NPS) and monthly logo churn metrics improve dramatically in the larger segments" [NL-012#NL-012-S03], and concludes that "mid-market and enterprise segments exhibit superior NPS (47 and 52, respectively) and strong expansion metrics, confirming the validity of the regulated enterprise ICP" [NL-015#NL-015-S03].
